idiom_name: abstract base + sealed cases + switch expression with a throwing default
implementation_notes: The pre-C# 15 realization closes the hierarchy structurally: an abstract base with a private constructor, one sealed type (plain class when the closure must be airtight, record for less ceremony) per case carrying its payload, and each operation a switch expression over the base type. Because the compiler's exhaustiveness analysis (CS8509/CS8524) covers enums but not sealed class hierarchies, every switch needs a _ => throw new UnreachableException() arm (.NET 7+; InvalidOperationException on the older runtimes that C# 9 targets), and the closure is held together by an analyser that suppresses CS8509 for provably closed hierarchies or by a test enumerating the cases; coverage is a build-quality property, not a language guarantee. The data modelling is identical to the C# 15 form, so migrating to closed hierarchies/unions is mechanical once the toolchain allows it.
pitfalls: CS8509 does not fire for sealed class hierarchies, so the _ arm is mandatory and silently swallows a case added later unless a suppressor/analyser or an explicit test guards the closure (Roslyn #64497, csharplang #7854).

Record hierarchies are not airtight closures: the compiler-generated protected copy constructor lets another assembly derive from a record base, which is why closed-hierarchy analysers exclude records by default.
UnreachableException fires at run time and only when the arm is actually evaluated, so a stale assembly compiled before a case was added fails late.

variants.name: Closed class hierarchy / union type with compiler-checked exhaustiveness (C# 15)
variants.idiom_name: closed record class hierarchy (or union type) + exhaustive switch expression
variants.implementation_notes: C# 15 (.NET 11) makes the closure declarative: public closed record class PaymentEvent restricts direct derivation to the declaring assembly, and the compiler then treats the known derived types as a complete list, so a switch expression covering all of them is exhaustive with no discard arm; union types extend the same guarantee to case types that are not related by inheritance. Adding a case produces non-exhaustiveness diagnostics at every switch that does not handle it. Use this form as soon as the toolchain allows it, and keep the analyser-backed pre-15 structure only for older target frameworks.
pitfalls: closed is an assembly-level contract: if another team must derive from the base, the hierarchy cannot be closed and the exhaustiveness analysis does not apply (the C# 15 proposals also add closed enums for the same reason).
The feature is new - preview at the time of writing - so reference assemblies and tooling must be current, and older target frameworks silently fall back to warning-level checks.

Union cases are type-level only (the Value property is unwrapped automatically); patterns other than null/_ apply to Value, so a union of nullable case types still needs explicit null handling for exhaustiveness.
